# Working here

This file is generated from a template shared by every repository its owner
maintains, and it is meant to improve. If anything below is wrong, unclear,
misleading, longer than it needs to be, or does not apply here, say so in the
chat — plainly, where it will be read, not as a footnote at the end of a long
answer. Say the same for anything that left you stuck, guessing, reading one
instruction twice, or spending tokens on work this file could have saved you.
Name what you would change and where: a fix to the template reaches every
repository, a fix to `AGENTS/` stays here.

That is a request, not an invitation to editorialise. Report what actually
cost you something.

## Starting work

- Pull `main` and branch from it. Name the branch after the work, prefixed `feat/`, `fix/` or `chore/` if possible.
  These branch rules win over any branch a session is assigned.
- Merging deletes the branch. The next piece of work is a new branch off
  `main` with a name of its own — never the same one again, and never more
  commits on the one that merged.
- One branch and one pull request at a time — one thing at a time, in this
  repository, in this conversation. Keep working on that branch until it is
  merged, then start again from `main`. Somebody else's pull request here,
  or your own in another repository, is not in the way: a change spanning
  two repositories is two pull requests.
- A new idea that arrives while a pull request is open belongs in that
  pull request if it fits, and on `docs/roadmap.md` if it is bigger than it.
  Not in a second branch.
- While a branch is open, leave `main` alone. Do not go looking for what
  has changed on it, and do not merge it in. Reconciling is its own
  instruction, and you will be given it when it is wanted. Where the pull
  request stops being mergeable, say so and stop — that is the instruction
  arriving, and it is not yours to give yourself.
- Once the pull request has merged, `main` is yours to read again: see
  [The next step](#the-next-step).

## Cross-repo dependencies

A scheduled run bumps every repository's dependencies every six hours, so a
fix merged here reaches the repositories that use it without help. Don't
bump, vendor or open a pull request elsewhere just to pass it on. Do, where
the work in hand cannot go on without the fix.

## Committing

- `make ready` passes before every commit. It regenerates what the
  generators own, fixes and formats what it can, then vets and runs the
  tests. It needs no network beyond the module cache, so it runs in a
  sandbox. `make tools` installs what it shells out to, and the Makefile
  puts that directory on its own `PATH`, so you do not have to.
- Because it regenerates, it may leave changes of its own. Those are its
  output, not a failure: read them, and commit them with the work where they
  follow from it, or on their own where they are drift an earlier run left
  behind.
- `make all` adds `govulncheck`, which reads the vulnerability database over
  the network. Run it where you have one; say so where you do not.
- A pull request runs `.github/workflows/test.yml`: golangci-lint, then the
  tests with the race detector. It is generated whole, so a check of your own
  goes in a workflow beside it.
- One commit per piece of work, not one per session.
- Push each commit as soon as it is made.
- Open the pull request yourself once there is something to review. Do not
  wait to be asked for it.

## Generated files

Edit the directory, never the file:

- `AGENTS.md` → `AGENTS/`
- `README.md` → `README/`
- `Makefile` → `mk/`

`.gitignore` is the exception: only the marked block at its head is
generated. Your own rules go below that block, where they win — in a
`.gitignore` the last matching pattern decides.

## Keeping the documents true

- Say what is, concisely. Not what was or how it came to be: that is git's.
  A warning against a trap says what to do and why.
- `README/*.md` is the README. If it no longer describes this repository,
  correcting it is part of the work, not a separate errand.
- `docs/architecture.md` describes the architecture as it stands. Update it
  in the same commit that changes the architecture.
- `mk/*.mk` is where a make target goes.
- `AGENTS/*.md` is this file's repository-specific half, and is held to the
  same standard: true, worth the reading, and never a restatement of what is
  above. A fragment that repeats the generated text costs every reader twice
  and drifts from it the first time the template changes. Say so rather than
  leaving one in place.

## The roadmap

`docs/roadmap.md`, with the files in `docs/roadmap/` it links to, is what
will be: the work not yet done, and nothing else. The owner adds plans and
ideas to it outside any conversation.

- A pull request that implements an item removes it in the same pull
  request: the whole entry or file, or the part that is done.
- An item you find already implemented, by earlier work or by the owner,
  goes too, in the pull request at hand.
- Where part of an item still says something true about the repository,
  move it into the document that describes what is, such as
  `docs/architecture.md` or `README/`, rewritten to say what is. Otherwise
  delete it. Keep no record of what was done: that is git's.
- Work worth doing outside the current change goes here, rather than
  widening the change.

## Code

- Comments are one line, and only where the code would otherwise puzzle a
  reader. Never a restatement of what it already says.
- Fail at startup when something required is missing, such as an
  environment variable, rather than fall back to a default.
- Keep one way to do each thing.
- Linters, scanners and generators are installed at their latest by
  `make tools`, and `devtool.json` pins the versions installed. A run moves
  a pin up, never back. Do not vendor one or add it to `go.mod` to run it.
- Check a claim before writing it down: read the source, run the command.
- Ask before making a decision that is the owner's — scope, or which of two
  designs. Do not ask about the process above; follow it.

## Reviews

- Reply to review feedback in the conversation with whoever raised it, not as
  a comment on the pull request.
- Resolve a thread once you have acted on it.
- Watching a pull request costs nothing, so do not spend a turn subscribing
  or unsubscribing and do not ask which is wanted. If it happens by itself,
  leave it. You will be told when there is a review to act on.

## The next step

End every piece of work — a pull request opened, a review answered, a pull
request merged — with the next step, in the chat. It keeps the project
moving towards what this repository is for, as `README/` says, by naming the
one thing that matters most now.

- **A question is open:** ask it, again if it went unanswered.
- **A pull request needs more:** say what it needs.
- **A pull request is ready:** suggest merging it, with its link.
- **A pull request has merged:** pull `main` and read what changed on it
  besides your work. The owner changes the roadmap and the code outside the
  conversation. Then suggest the top one to three ways forward, from the
  roadmap or from what would close off the work just done.

It is a nudge, not an analysis. Do not rethink it each time: the same
suggestion again is fine, and wanted, until the owner answers it.
